This is a reading-layout fixture. It lives outside the article collection and is
only copied into a temporary build during browser checks. It is not a blog post.

## A readable paragraph

An article needs enough room for a complete thought. This paragraph checks the
reading column, line spacing, and the distance between paragraphs. Its purpose
is to expose cramped layouts at large screen sizes and overflowing text on a
small phone. The surrounding page should remain easy to scan.

A second paragraph checks the vertical rhythm. A reader should see where one
thought ends and the next begins without encountering a large empty gap. This
line also contains an [ordinary link](https://example.com) and an inline
`identifier` so the text styles can be checked together.

### A smaller heading

The smaller heading should be distinct from the paragraph but quieter than a
section heading.

## Code stays in its own frame

```typescript title="example.ts"
const message = "A sample copied from this block only";
const deliberatelyLongLine = "This line is intentionally long enough to require horizontal scrolling on a small phone while the rest of the article stays inside the page.";
console.log(message);
```

## Lists keep their spacing

- The first item checks spacing next to a paragraph.
- The second item checks the gap between list items.
- The last item checks the transition back to ordinary text.

1. A numbered list keeps its visible order.
2. A second entry checks the marker alignment.

## A short quotation

> This quotation checks the border, background, and paragraph spacing. It is test
> text, not an attribution to a person.

## A table can scroll

| Element | Small screen | Large screen |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Paragraph | Remains inside the viewport | Uses a comfortable line length |
| Code and table | Scroll inside their own frame | Fit within the reading column |
| Contents | Opens when requested | Leaves the article at full width |

## A second code block

```java title="Example.java"
System.out.println("A different code sample.");
```

The final paragraph checks the end of the article. There should be a clear gap
before the previous and next links, with no subscription panel or fixed overlay.
